title: What If You Went Outside With Wet Hair in Winter?

scenes.text: What if you walked out into winter with wet hair? Your grandma was half right.
Cold air can't give you a cold by itself. Colds come from viruses, mostly rhinovirus.
But in 2005, Cardiff scientists had ninety people sit with their feet in cold water for twenty minutes.
Over the next five days, they were about two to three times as likely to get cold symptoms as people who stayed warm.
Chilling narrows blood vessels in your nose, and Yale found cold viruses copy themselves better in a cooler nose.
So the cold doesn't bring the virus. It may wake up the one already hiding in you.
